question.text: The magnitude of projection of line joining $(3,4$, $5)$ and $(4,6,3)$ on the line joining $(-1,2,4)$ and $(1,0,5)$ is

solution.text:
We know that, projection of $\mathbf{a}$ on $\mathbf{b}$ is given by projection, $|\mathrm{a}| \cos \theta=\frac{(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b})}{|\mathbf{b}|}$
Let line joining points $(3,4,5)$ and $(4,6,3)$ is $L_1$ and line joining points $(-1,2,4)$ and $(1,0,5)$ is $L_2$
$\Rightarrow \quad \begin{aligned}
& L_1=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\
& L_2=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}
\end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ Projection of $L_1$ and $L_2=\frac{L_1 \cdot L_2}{\left|L_2\right|}$
$=\frac{2-4-2}{\sqrt{4+4+1}}=\frac{-4}{3}$
$\therefore$ Magnitude $=\frac{4}{3}$
